formulas.loss: Flow does not depend on fill height (true once the fill exceeds about 1.2 silo diameters, by the Janssen effect) or on silo diameter (when it exceeds 2.5 D and D + 30 d). C and k are fitted per material and must come with their source; the kernel has no default for either. Mono-sized dry grains above 0.5 mm. formulas.formula: s(t)^2 = e^2 + sigma(t)^2; f(t) = exp(-(a - mu(t))^2 / (2 s(t)^2)) / s(t); density = f / (sum f * step); highest-density region at L = cells with probability >= the threshold where the sorted cells first reach L
formulas.loss: One age, one curve, no priors: the result is the likelihood normalised on the grid, which is the posterior only under a uniform prior on the grid (a Bayesian model with phases or sequences needs more priors). The curve is linear between its points, and its errors are taken as independent from point to point; IntCal20's own covariance is not used. Density beyond the grid ends is dropped (the grid is refused when an end holds more than 1e-6 of the peak). exp below -700 is taken as 0. A highest-density region is a set of grid cells, so its ends are known to one grid step. Reservoir offsets, mixed curves and the post-bomb range are not handled.
